terms.definition: AWS's Content Delivery Network (CDN) service that caches content at 400+ edge locations worldwide to reduce latency for global users
terms.example: Like setting up local chai stalls in every city so nobody has to travel to the factory in Mumbai

terms.definition: Content Delivery Network — a distributed system of servers that cache content near end users to improve speed and reduce load on the origin server
terms.example: Netflix uses a CDN so movies stream fast in every country

terms.definition: A mini data center operated by AWS in a city where CloudFront caches content. Distinct from regions and AZs — there are 400+ edge locations worldwide
terms.example: AWS has edge locations in Chennai, Delhi, Sydney, London, etc.

terms.definition: The source of truth for CloudFront — the original storage location of your content, such as an S3 bucket, EC2 instance, or Application Load Balancer
terms.example: S3 bucket in Mumbai is the origin; CloudFront fetches from it on cache misses

terms.definition: A CloudFront delivery configuration that maps an origin to a globally distributed endpoint URL (e.g., d111abc.cloudfront.net)
terms.example: Creating a distribution is like telling CloudFront 'serve content from this S3 bucket to the whole world'

terms.definition: Origin Access Control — a CloudFront security mechanism that allows only a specific CloudFront distribution to access a private S3 bucket, replacing the older OAI
terms.example: OAC means your bucket stays private but CloudFront can still read from it on behalf of users

terms.definition: Origin Access Identity — the older, deprecated mechanism for allowing CloudFront to access private S3 buckets. Replaced by OAC for new distributions
terms.example: OAI is like an old security badge — still works but no longer recommended

terms.definition: When a user requests content and CloudFront already has it cached at the nearest edge location — served instantly without contacting the origin
terms.example: After the first user in Sydney loads an image, all subsequent Sydney users get a cache hit

terms.definition: When CloudFront doesn't have the requested content cached — it must fetch from the origin, store it, then serve it. Slower than a cache hit
terms.example: The very first request for a new file is always a cache miss

terms.definition: Time to Live — how long (in seconds) CloudFront keeps content cached at edge locations before fetching a fresh copy from origin. Default is 86400 seconds (24 hours)
terms.example: Setting TTL=3600 means images are refreshed from S3 every hour

terms.definition: AWS's authoritative Domain Name System (DNS) service. Translates human-friendly domain names (e.g., mysite.com) into IP addresses or AWS resource endpoints
terms.example: Like the internet's phone book — you look up 'myshop.com' and Route 53 tells you where to find it

terms.definition: A container in Route 53 that holds all DNS records for a specific domain (e.g., myshop.com). Created automatically when you register a domain through Route 53
terms.example: Creating a hosted zone for myshop.com lets you add A records, CNAME records, MX records, etc.

terms.definition: A DNS record type that maps a domain name to an IPv4 address. In Route 53, can also be an Alias record pointing to AWS resources like CloudFront or ELB
terms.example: www.myshop.com → 203.45.67.89 (standard A record) or → d111abc.cloudfront.net (Alias A record)

terms.definition: A Route 53 extension of the A record that can target AWS resource endpoints (CloudFront, ALB, S3) by DNS name rather than IP. Free per query and auto-updates on IP changes
terms.example: Points myshop.com to your CloudFront distribution; no static IP needed

terms.definition: The time it takes for DNS record changes to spread across all DNS resolvers worldwide. Can take minutes to 48 hours depending on TTL settings
terms.example: After changing name servers, some users see the new site while others still see the old one during propagation

terms.definition: The official AWS SDK (Software Development Kit) for Python. Allows Python code to create, configure, and manage AWS services programmatically
terms.example: A Python script using Boto3 can launch 100 EC2 instances in seconds — no console clicking needed

terms.definition: Software Development Kit — a set of libraries provided by AWS for different programming languages so developers can interact with AWS services from their application code
terms.example: Available for Python (Boto3), JavaScript, Java, Go, Ruby, .NET, and more

terms.definition: Amazon Machine Image — a template that defines the operating system, configuration, and software for an EC2 instance. AMI IDs are region-specific
terms.example: ami-0c55b159cbfafe1f0 might be Ubuntu Server in ap-south-1 but has a different ID in us-east-1

terms.definition: A CloudFront operation that forces edge locations to remove cached objects before TTL expires. Use /* to invalidate all files. First 1,000 paths/month are free
terms.example: After deploying a new website version, invalidate /* so users get the new files immediately

terms.definition: A Route 53 routing policy that uses health checks to automatically route traffic to a backup (secondary) resource when the primary becomes unhealthy
terms.example: Primary site in ap-south-1 goes down — Route 53 automatically switches users to backup in us-east-1

terms.definition: A Route 53 routing policy that distributes traffic between multiple resources according to assigned percentage weights
terms.example: Send 90% of traffic to v1 and 10% to v2 for A/B testing a new feature

terms.definition: A Route 53 routing policy that routes users to the AWS region providing them the lowest network latency — ideal for multi-region deployments
terms.example: Users in Australia automatically go to ap-southeast-2 instead of us-east-1

terms.definition: An S3 feature that allows S3 to serve HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files directly as a website via an S3 endpoint URL, without needing a web server
terms.example: Store index.html in S3, enable static website hosting, and S3 serves it like a web server
